name: Stuart Duncan
notes: The Nashville session fiddle bench's first call for this archetype. The section's own scope note says why this entry looks the way it does: "in this archetype the producer role is largely occupied by instrumental specialists — the players whose parts are the train beat when there is no drum kit, and who also produce records. Each entry below is written as a parameter set for the part they contribute, because that is what the engine needs." His part is specified as two modes: "the fiddle's role in the train beat is a continuous sawed 8th- or 16th-note stream on the up-tempo material (this is the old-time function, distinct from the bluegrass fiddle's break-taking function), so model two fiddle modes: rhythm fiddle = unbroken subdivision with drone double-stops; lead fiddle = 8- or 16-bar break with scalar runs and sliding thirds." Both are authored inside one model rather than as `modes`, because the parent genre supplies three moods that authoring modes would delete: rhythm fiddle is the continuous 16th hat stream and the 7–13 melody density, lead fiddle is the 8–16 bar bridge and the countermelody's answer_lick share. Keys are the stated fiddle-native A, D, G, E "and their relative minors, where open-string drones are available", so B minor and E minor carry a small weight beside them. His documented classical training and jazz-violin work mean "chromatic and altered vocabulary is in-palette where the arrangement asks for it", which is `extensions.ninth` 0.06 and a ii–V–I family — modest, because the entry says in-palette rather than characteristic. The "double-stop pads under vocals as a steel-guitar substitute" is the sustain_pad share at `densityRatio` 0.6, and the "answer-phrase fills in 2-bar units" is `phraseBars` weighted to 2. The drum block is the drummerless wing's: `kick` [1,2] on anchors 1 and 3, brush-range velocities, `snare.offGridMs` −5 for the anticipated placement, `percs` at −10 dB. ⚠ The entry states "the two-mode parameterisation formalised from convention [LOW-CONF]", and that flag applies to the hat stream and the melody density above. ⚠ Also INFERRED: the tempo band — the entry says only "BPM whole archetype range", so 80–210 with `mode` 150 is this author's reading of the grammar block's own stated bands (80–95 cut time through 180–210 breakdown) rather than a number from his entry. ⚠ Also INFERRED: velocity tiers, `percs` contents and every bassline number.
